title: Rogers–Szegő local ordinary discriminants and arithmetic
plain_meaning: Describes exactly how repeated Rogers–Szegő roots split when q moves away from a fixed root of unity, including the extra collision at −1, and computes the first nonzero ordinary discriminant coefficient.
exact_claim:
Let H_n(z;q)=sum_k [n choose k]_q z^k, D_n(q)=Disc_z H_n, n=Ad+b, d odd, ω primitive of order d, and q(ε)=ω(1+ε²)^(1/d). Put F=z^d+1 and P_A=product_(j=1)^A j^j.
Separated case: G=H_b(z;ω), 0≤b<d, A≥1, Disc(G)Res(F,G)≠0. At α^d=−1, H_n(α+εx;q(ε))=ε^A(−1)^A d^(A/2)G(α)He_A(√d x/α)+O(ε^(A+1)). With K=dA(A−1)/2, D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2K)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2)P_A^d Disc(G)Res(F,G)^(2A). Thus ord_(Φ_d)D_n=K.
Simple-overlap case: d≥3, b odd with 1≤b<d. Write G=(z+1)U, g=U(−1), W=(ω;ω)_b/(ω²;ω²)_((b+d)/2), τ=dW/g and J_(A+1)=He_(A+1)+A(1−τ)He_(A−1). If g≠0, H_n(−1+εx;q(ε))=ε^(A+1)(−1)^(A+1)d^((A−1)/2)g J_(A+1)(−√d x;τ)+O(ε^(A+2)).
If additionally Disc(U)Res(F,U)Disc(J_(A+1))≠0, L=dA(A−1)/2+A and D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2L)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2+A)P_A^(d−1)Disc(J_(A+1))Disc(U)Res(F,U)^(2A)g². Hence ord_(Φ_d)D_n=L. Square roots cancel coefficientwise.
model: Characteristic-zero formal series; ordinary z-derivative discriminant; arbitrary fixed odd d with the stated residual guards. Disc(1)=1.
proof_status: Both separated and overlap theorems were accepted in saved independent audits. This catalogue re-read the proofs and qualifications, but did not repeat their computations or create a fresh independent correctness audit.
inspection_status: Theorem/audit source read as inert text; no supplied program execution
novelty_status: Plausible specific theorem package; external priority remains unresolved. Standard q-Lucas, Hermite limits, quasi-Laguerre discriminants and hook-Wronskian theory are not new.
novelty_delta: The narrow candidate is the explicitly normalized fixed-nontrivial-ω, moving-z local coefficient, especially τ and the shared-root coefficient, together with its full ordinary discriminant and arithmetic use.
significance: Ranks first in this domain: uniform exact formulas with independent proof audits, coherent special-functions/arithmetic consequences, and a more visible substantive increment than isolated certificate or standard-ingredient applications.
publication_readiness: Best algebra manuscript-development core; needs self-contained exposition and legitimate full-text priority comparisons, especially Lubinsky–Saff 1987 and Zhedanov 1997. No originality announcement warranted.
limitations: Only separated or exactly one simple shared residual root at −1. Nonzero residual discriminant/resultant and Disc J are essential. No arbitrary-overlap, repeated-p, all-composite, or globally cleared novelty theorem.
rank_rationale: The strongest coherent specialized mathematical package: growing-degree local coefficients, exact ordinary-discriminant leading terms and arithmetic consequences. Its fixed-root local increment is precise; two close older full-text comparisons remain open.

title: Exact scalar common-cycle chirp-resolvent bank minima
plain_meaning: Determines the fewest first-order resolvents of one fixed cycle needed to synthesize an odd quadratic chirp, and how one free diagonal changes that answer.
exact_claim:
For N=2m+1≥3, primitive q in characteristic zero, h=(N+1)/2, f(k)=q^(hk²), C=sum_(k=0)^(N−1)f(k)P^k, represent C=sum_(s=1)^Q a_s(I−λ_sP)^(−1), with a_s,λ_s≠0 and λ_s^N≠1. Without a free diagonal Qmin=m+1 for every odd N.
With δI free, Qmin=m iff T_m(z)=(-1)^mH_m(−z;q) has simple nonzero nonresonant roots; otherwise Qmin=m+1. An arbitrary free diagonal does not enlarge this scalar common-P circulant model.
T_m(0)=(-1)^m. gcd(T_m,z^N−1)=1 for N≡1 mod4 and z−1 for N≡3 mod4, the latter root simple. Thus all N≡3 mod4 have Qmin=m+1. Every prime N≡1 mod4 and the audited infinite families have Qmin=m.
When Qmin=m, δ=(-1)^m q^(−m(m+1)/2)product_(j=1)^m(1−q^j) is forced and nonzero. Nodes/weights may lie in an algebraic closure; root-free sum works over Q(q).

title: Universal reciprocal Hankel/diagonal-pencil resultant factors
plain_meaning: Extracts universal factors and reciprocal symmetry from a family of determinant resultants, substantially reducing interpolation degree.

w^T R(1/w)=(−1)^(m²)R(w); R=w^v(w−1)^(m²)U; w^(2b)U(1/w)=U(w); U=w^bV(w+w^(−1)) with deg V≤b.
The accepted adjacent-Hankel theorem is A_ij=T_(i+j), B_ij=T_(i+j+1), m=s+1. Universal identities survive singular, leading-coefficient-drop, and zero-resultant specializations. Generic w=0 valuation is exact; specialization may raise it.
